name: New Towns Taskforce report to government
fact: Published 28 September 2025; independent Taskforce report recommends potential locations and delivery approaches for the next generation of new towns in England.
gate: Taskforce recommendations are not final designations, permissions, land assembly decisions or exact canonical parcel relations.

name: Initial government response to New Towns Taskforce
fact: Government welcomed all 12 recommended locations; the shortlist mixed urban extensions, regeneration and standalone settlements with potential for up to 300,000 homes over coming decades.
gate: The response explicitly preceded final site decisions; shortlist membership is not adopted planning status or parcel-level growth certainty.

name: New Towns Draft Programme consultation
fact: Published 23 March 2026; consultation covered 7 proposed locations, delivery/planning policy and Strategic Environmental Assessment, with final proposals intended after consultation and assessments.
gate: Draft programme status must not be represented as confirmed final designation or development consent.

name: New Towns Draft Programme detailed policy
fact: The 2026 draft programme lists seven proposed locations and identifies Crews Hill and Chase Park, Leeds South Bank and Tempsford as priority interventions receiving significant government focus.
gate: Priority intervention status is strategic programme evidence, not exact parcel inclusion, delivery date, viability or permission.

name: New Towns locations methodology
fact: Annex C, published 23 March 2026, documents the assessment methodology used to evaluate potential New Town locations.
gate: Methodology supports provenance and screening only; it is not a final location decision or parcel-scoring substitute.

name: Seven new towns proposed press release
fact: Published 22 March 2026; seven locations were proposed, each expected to deliver at least 10,000 homes, with several at up to 40,000 or more over coming decades.
gate: Proposed scale is programme-level and conditional on consultation, environmental assessment, planning and delivery arrangements.

name: New Towns Taskforce terms of reference
fact: Terms require recommendations to support economic growth and housing demand while considering viability, sustainability, affordability and reasonable delivery timeframes.
gate: Selection criteria do not establish that any particular canonical parcel satisfies them.

name: National Housing Delivery Fund — MHCLG
fact: Published 31 March 2026; NHDF provides capital funding for infrastructure and land to support the ambition for 1.5 million homes and accelerate additional housing supply.
gate: Fund existence or geographic eligibility does not prove a specific site has an award, viable business case or funded infrastructure.

name: National Housing Delivery Fund — Homes England
fact: NHDF can support land assembly, remediation and upfront infrastructure such as utilities and schools for housing and mixed-use projects, prioritising early delivery and housing need.
gate: Available support is not evidence that a named site has funding, land control or delivery certainty.

name: Homes England and National Housing Bank investment prospectus 2026
fact: Published 31 March 2026; up to £46bn is available over 10 years through Homes England and the National Housing Bank, including grant, infrastructure/land and debt/equity/guarantee products.
gate: Programme capital is not a site-level commitment; exact award, conditions, timing and parcel relation remain required.

name: National Housing Bank
fact: Established by Homes England and published 31 March 2026; the Bank provides purpose-built finance intended to accelerate housing delivery and regeneration across England.
gate: Finance availability does not establish borrower eligibility, approval or parcel-level development probability.

name: Homes England agency remit
fact: Homes England uses land, capital, partnerships and statutory powers to accelerate housebuilding and regeneration and support sustainable places.
gate: Agency remit is contextual only and cannot be translated into a site intervention without project evidence.

name: Homes England 2025-26 housebuilding statistics
fact: Published 25 June 2026; Homes England programmes recorded 42,433 starts and 40,332 completions in 2025-26, with 32,243 affordable completions.
gate: Programme-wide delivery counts are market/delivery context, not evidence for a canonical parcel.

name: Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36
fact: Current guidance states at least £27.3bn of government funding is available through Homes England for social and affordable homes outside London under SAHP 2026-36.
gate: National grant availability does not prove a site allocation, tenure mix, bid success or development timing.

name: SAHP Strategic Partnership guidance
fact: Guidance describes delivery thresholds and funding caps for strategic partners, including minimum delivery commitments extending to 31 March 2036.
gate: Applicant thresholds are programme rules and do not indicate whether a specific land parcel is in an approved programme.

name: Investment Zones in England
fact: Updated 15 April 2026; eight English areas were invited, seven final plans had been agreed, with interventions spanning planning, local infrastructure, innovation, skills and business support.
gate: Investment Zone economic-area membership is not the same as a designated tax site or parcel-level incentive eligibility.

name: Freeports technical handbook introduction
fact: HMRC handbook published 1 June 2026 lists eight English Freeports and explains that customs incentives apply within designated customs sites, not automatically across the whole Freeport area.
gate: Freeport geography alone does not establish customs-site status, tax-site status or development potential for a parcel.

name: Freeports programme guidance
fact: Government guidance describes Freeports as place-based areas intended to boost investment, innovation, trade, regeneration and long-term jobs using incentive packages and infrastructure.
gate: Programme objectives are strategic context; exact current boundaries, tax/customs designations and site eligibility must be separately verified.

name: Streamlining infrastructure planning implementation plan
fact: Published 23 March 2026; implementation plan links major electricity, roads, public transport and water infrastructure to economic growth and enabling 1.5 million homes.
gate: National process reform does not prove approval, funding, route or timing of infrastructure affecting a parcel.

name: National Framework for Water Resources 2025
fact: Updated 15 April 2026; framework estimates that without action public-water-supply deficit could reach up to 5bn litres/day by 2055 while population and housing growth increase demand.
gate: National/regional deficit is a constraint signal only; water-company capacity and network-level evidence are required for a site.

name: Water resources planning guideline 2026
fact: Updated 16 June 2026; WRMP guidance says plans should reflect local and strategic growth ambitions, including major housing/growth locations and new towns, when forecasting demand and infrastructure needs.
gate: Planning requirement does not establish spare capacity or a connection for any specific development.

name: Water demand Environment Act target delivery plan
fact: Updated 16 July 2026; England target is 20% lower public-water use per head by 2038, with interim per-head and leakage reductions for 2027 and 2032.
gate: Demand-management targets do not guarantee local supply headroom or remove site-specific water constraints.

name: NESO Connections Reform
fact: NESO reports reform of the previous queue into a delivery pipeline, prioritising ready and strategically aligned projects and stating 381.5GW of capacity has been unlocked.
gate: System-level pipeline reform is not a distribution-network capacity statement or connection offer for a parcel.

name: NESO About Connections Reform
fact: Gate 2 projects must satisfy readiness and strategic-alignment criteria to secure a confirmed connection date, point and queue position; Gate 1 does not provide a confirmed date.
gate: Energy-project Gate status cannot be inferred for a housing or employment site without the relevant connection agreement and network evidence.

name: NESO Connections Reform Results
fact: NESO says the former queue exceeded 700GW and the re-ordered pipeline prioritises projects that are ready and needed, with regional/technology results available for context.
gate: Regional pipeline context does not equal local substation capacity or a guaranteed connection for a development.

name: NESO Connections Reform timeline
fact: Timeline updated in 2026 sets phased offer windows through March 2027, with timing varying by protection status, transmission/distribution phase and engineering complexity.
gate: Programme-wide windows do not determine a specific project's offer date or site utility readiness.

name: NESO CM095 Implementing Connections Reform
fact: CM095 is marked implemented/concluded, last updated 12 January 2026, introducing processes intended to let the most ready projects progress more rapidly.
gate: Code implementation does not establish network capacity or connection rights at a site.

name: NESO Project Designation
fact: NESO states designated projects can receive a guaranteed place in the reformed queue if readiness requirements are met, with designation expected to be rare.
gate: Designation is exceptional and must never be assumed from project type, location or economic importance.

name: NESO readiness declaration
fact: Gate 2 applicants with existing agreements must submit evidence demonstrating readiness and strategic alignment through the prescribed declaration process.
gate: Evidence requirements do not show that a particular development has submitted, qualified or secured a connection.

name: Investment Opportunity Fund prospectus
fact: Official prospectus describes a fund to unlock specific named private investments in Freeports and Investment Zones, including targeted enabling works and viability support subject to criteria.
gate: The 2024 prospectus is programme context and does not prove a 2026 funding award, current availability or parcel-specific investment.
